## Maintainer ruling recorded — **(a)**: for an authored `type: 'kanban'` document the **plugin dialect is authoritative**. `@object-ui/types`' `'kanban'` arm (type + Zod mirror) is rewritten to declare exactly the shape `ObjectKanbanRenderer` reads (`objectName` / `groupBy` / `cardTitle` / `cardFields` / card `badges` … — the 18-member `KanbanSchema` `plugin-kanban` consumes), and `plugin-kanban` conforms to that declaration; the `DeclarativeKanban*` trio loses its only live consumer and retires under ADR-0049

Director seat, summon #14, session `session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um` (GitHub `os-warren`), 2026-09-05. Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat, decision batch #41 (item 4, presented with the recommendation (a) and the explicit note that it reverses the "keep both faces" half of the objectui#6172 ruling), verbatim reply 「同意」. Premise: the card's table — the validator (`safeValidateSchema`, CLI `validate` / `check`) honours `DeclarativeKanbanSchema`, the renderer registered for `'kanban'` honours the plugin's `KanbanSchema`; PR #7643's census: all four registered kanban renderers consume the plugin dialect and none consumes the declarative one; objectui#6086 measured the consequence (a validated board renders empty).

**Ruled: (a).** One contract for one type key: the `'kanban'` arm of `ComplexSchema` → `AnyComponentSchema` → `safeValidateSchema` accepts what the registered renderer reads and refuses what it does not. Dependency direction stays correct — `@object-ui/types` declares, `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` imports and conforms (it already depends on `types`). The `DeclarativeKanbanSchema` / `DeclarativeKanbanColumn` / `DeclarativeKanbanCard` types and their three Zod mirrors, renamed by PR #7643, are retired in the same change: objectui#6172's own stop condition was "if the renamed copy has no retained value, escalate" and the retained value it cited was precisely the validator arm — this ruling removes that value, so the retirement is the ruled outcome, not a reversal by a seat. Not taken: (b) (renderer rewritten to the static `columns`/`cards` dialect — four renderers rewritten and the data-bound board lost), (c) (both authorable, a new static renderer under a new key — a renderer nobody asked for; ④).

**Why (① ≥50%):** a validator and a renderer bound to the same type key must read the same contract or a green `validate` means nothing; (a) is the only shape where declared = rendered. ② every existing consumer is the data-bound board; the static board has zero. ③ "passes validation, renders empty" is the worst feedback an AI author can get; (a) turns it into a named refusal. ④ one dialect fewer.

**Execution:** `domain:ui` seat, M, `packages/types` (`complex.ts`, `zod/complex.zod.ts`, `index.ts`, `zod/index.zod.ts`, `registry.ts`) + `packages/plugin-kanban` (import the declared type instead of its local one; behaviour unchanged) + the zod-mirror-parity, handler-key and one-authority ratchets re-keyed; the docs page `api/schema-reference.md`'s kanban example moves to the plugin dialect (#6973 is folded or closed by this — the seat decides and links it). Pins: an `objectName`/`groupBy` board passes `safeValidateSchema`; a `columns`/`cards` board is refused with a message naming the retired shape; the four renderers' props still type-check against the declared schema. **`Clause-②: yes`** ⇒ `needs:contract-review` on the PR, parked for the director. Changeset: `@object-ui/types` **minor** with a BREAKING banner — the `'kanban'` validator arm's accept set is replaced and the six `DeclarativeKanban*` exports (renamed by #7643 in the same release line) are retired, stated as the second step of that rename; `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` patch. Sequencing: after #7651 (ruled B in the same batch — no data ladder, so `data?: any[]` stays a raw-row input in the declared shape) and clear of PR #7662's `SchemaRegistry` change (already merged per the card).

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. `finding` · `domain:ui` unchanged. Ledger: objectstack #12708, batch #41. Related: objectui#6172 · #7645 · #7651 · #6086 · #6973 · PR #7643 · PR #7662.

## Sequencing correction before this card is dispatched — PR #7662 has **not** merged

The ruling's Execution paragraph reads:

> Sequencing: after #7651 (ruled B in the same batch …) and clear of PR #7662's `SchemaRegistry` change (**already merged per the card**).

The first half holds — #7651 is closed `not_planned` (2026-09-05T02:09:54Z). The second half does not. Read from the API just now:

| | reading |
| :-- | :-- |
| PR #7662 state | **open**, **draft**, `merged: false` |
| mergeable_state | `behind` |
| gate | carrying a **second** contract-review REFUSE (comment 5548793740) |

So `registry.ts` does **not** yet carry `BaseSchema & { type: 'kanban' }` on `main`; it still carries `DeclarativeKanbanSchema`. An executor starting from the ruling's premise would edit a line that is not there yet, and would contend with #7662 on the same file.

Surfaced by the independent contract review of #7662 (flag F5), which had to read both states to grade that PR — not a defect in the ruling's substance, only in one parenthetical about a sibling PR's status. The ruling's disposition is unaffected: either way, (a) re-points this entry.

**Disposition from the `domain:ui` seat: this card is NOT dispatched yet.** It is held until PR #7662 lands, for two reasons that are the ruling's own:

1. Both changes edit `packages/types/src/registry.ts`, and #7662's outstanding remediation touches the comment at `:201` that (a) will rewrite.
2. #7662's entry is the *transitional* state under (a). Landing them out of order means the executor writes the final state onto a file whose intermediate state is still in review, and the review record for #7662 stops describing any tree that ever existed.

⛔ Not an indefinite park. #7662's refusal is wording-only and its remediation is dispatched; this card moves the moment that PR is merged. It stays `pm:queue` so it is visible in the pool meanwhile.

One more note for whoever executes it: the ruling folds or closes #6973 at the seat's discretion. #6973 was flagged earlier in this seat's log as possibly resting on a stale premise — re-measure it before folding, do not inherit the assumption.

## ✅ Hold lifted — PR #7662 has merged. This card is dispatchable now.

I held this card on 2026-09-05T02:39Z (comment 5548799174) because the ruling's sequencing note said PR #7662 was "already merged per the card" and it was not. That is now resolved by the fact, not by a re-reading:

**PR #7662 merged 2026-09-05T07:14:56Z as `bc640ec56`** (`merged: true` read from the API, `Fixes #7645`, card closed). It landed after **three** contract-review rounds; the third returned PASS.

### The exact state ruling (a)'s executor inherits — read from `main`, not from a report

`origin/main` `bc640ec56`, `packages/types/src/registry.ts`:

```ts
'kanban': BaseSchema & { type: 'kanban' };
```

⛔ So do **not** start from `DeclarativeKanbanSchema`. The entry is the transitional form, and (a) re-points this one line at the declared type.

The #7662 contract review enumerated the rest of the inheritance, and judged it does **not** pre-empt any part of (a):

- the **one type line** above;
- the `BaseSchema` import at `registry.ts:9`, which becomes unused after the re-point — a tidy, not a gate (`noUnusedLocals: false`, `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` is `warn`);
- the comment block at `registry.ts:187-217`, whose "⛔ Do not restore … without moving the renderer's dialect into a layer this package may depend on" names (a)'s route rather than forbidding it;
- both pin test files, which import `DeclarativeKanbanSchema` and therefore **retire with the trio** — disclosed in their own docblocks. The reviewer flagged `_KeyKept` as worth carrying forward.

### Two numbers in the ruling that the executor should NOT inherit

- The ruling says "the 18-member `KanbanSchema`". The measured body count is **19** (AST census, controls lit). Re-derive rather than trusting either number.
- The ruling folds or closes objectui#6973 at the seat's discretion. #6973 was flagged in this seat's log as possibly resting on a stale premise — **re-measure it before folding**, do not inherit the assumption.

### Also cleared since the ruling was written

- **#7651** — closed `not_planned` (ruled B in the same batch). The fence it named is gone.
- **#6172** — closed `completed` by PR #7643. Its "keep both faces" half is what (a) reverses; the ruling says so explicitly.

Card stays `pm:queue`, unassigned. `Clause-②: yes` per the ruling, so whoever takes it owes a draft PR with `needs:contract-review` on **both** carriers, and a `minor` changeset with a BREAKING banner.

## Contract review (clause ②), fresh and full after the R1 REFUSE — **PASS** — PR #7743 at head `1a5915f2`

Director seat, summon #15, `session_01TezFG8ZMrNH6n5VTNpPpdH` (`os-zhuang`), 2026-09-05T16:2xZ, on the maintainer's instruction 「然后执行契约复审」. This is a new review of the whole 25-file remediated diff at `1a5915f2`, not a re-read of the REFUSE (5552425067) — that verdict's findings were used only as an attack list. Readings are this seat's own, taken from the PR head fetched as `refs/pull/7743/head` and from objectui `origin/main` `737037f2`.

Reviewed-by: `session_01TezFG8ZMrNH6n5VTNpPpdH`

### ① Derived judgments — accept set and public face

| # | claim | this seat's reading | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| R1 | `onCardClick` is a declared **runtime slot** on the `'kanban'` arm: callable on the TS face, refused by name on the mirror | PR head `packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts:152`: `onCardClick: handlerKeyRefusal('onCardClick', 'runtime-slot', 'Card click handler')` beside `onCardMove` (:151) and `onQuickAdd` (:155) — a declared refusing arm, so `BaseSchema`'s `.passthrough()` no longer keeps the value. TS face `complex.ts`: `onCardClick?: (card: KanbanCard, event?: unknown) => void`. The widening the REFUSE measured is closed at the source, not only at the probe. | correct |
| R1-disp | runtime-slot rather than retired | objectui `origin/main` `plugin-kanban/src/index.tsx:194` forwards `onCardClick={schema.onCardClick}` in the same block as the two kept slots; `ObjectKanban.tsx:151` declares an `onCardClick` prop and `:938-940` its substitute **calls** the authored one. An authored `onCardClick` on a `type: 'kanban'` document runs ⇒ live on every channel measured; `retired` would have declared a live key dead. | correct |
| 2 | Ledger re-keyed: `RUNTIME_SLOT` 44 → 45, `ALL_SITES` 66 → 67, `RETIRED` 22 unchanged; `KeepsFunction<KanbanSchema['onCardClick']>` type assertion | Diff of `handler-keys-json-refusal-6124.test.ts`: `toHaveLength(45)` / `toHaveLength(22)` / `new Set(ids).size).toBe(67)`, the `onCardClick` row re-keyed to `KanbanSchema`, and the `Expect<KeepsFunction<…>>` line present. The dev's ablation (`?: never` back in ⇒ TS2344 at that line + TS2322 in `zod-mirror-parity`) shows the type instrument is lit. | correct |
| 3 | The `'kanban'` arm declares the plugin dialect (19 live members + `onCardClick` + 3 tombstones `draggable` / `onColumnAdd` / `onCardAdd`; column `color?: never`); `registry.ts` `'kanban': KanbanSchema`; six `DeclarativeKanban*` exports removed | Mirror hunk read: `KanbanSchema = BaseSchema.extend({...})` with `draggable: retiredDeclarativeKanbanKey(...)`, `onColumnAdd` / `onCardAdd` as `'retired'` arms; `index.ts` exports `KanbanCard`, `KanbanColumn`, `KanbanSchema`. Whole-name removal for the six exports is right — a whole exported name has no carrier to tombstone, and the retirement is the ruling's own outcome (objectui#6172's stop condition). | correct |
| 4 | No remaining consumer of the retired names | `git grep DeclarativeKanban` on objectui / cloud / hotcrm `origin/main` outside the PR's own files: two historical `.changeset` entries and one **comment** line in `scripts/check-doc-links.mjs:508` (no code reference). Zero live importers. | correct |
| 5 | `plugin-kanban/src/types.ts` becomes a re-export of the five declared types; behaviour unchanged | Files list −218/+31 on that file, `ObjectKanban.tsx` import becomes `import type`; the plugin's public type names are preserved through the re-export. | correct |
| 6 | Refusal pin re-read as A (refuse `draggable` and column `color`, not `columns[].cards[]`) | The plugin dialect declares `columns[].cards[]` and `bucketCardsIntoColumns` pushes raw records into `cards`, so refusing card field names would refuse the declaration itself; A executes the ruling's principle (accept what the registered renderer reads). The REFUSE reviewer reached the same answer independently. | correct |

### ② semver
